main_text.p: Exemplar verò secuti sumus Antuerpiense, collatis insuper vetustis quibusdam MSS. Bibliis, & aliis melioris notæ impressis, Venetis, Basileensibus aliisque, etiam Manassis Ben Israel, nuper Amstelodami ab ipso magnâ diligentiâ editis. Distinctionem verò capitum & versuum ab Ecclesiâ hodiè receptam secuti sumus, omissis Iudæorum Parashis & Sidris, de quibus tamen in Apparatu. Varias verò lectiones, seu Keri, & Ketib, cum jetir, & Chaser, &c. de quarum origine, usu, numero, &c. magnâ hodiè inter doctos agitantur controversiæ (de quibus cū aliis ad Majoram spectantibus in Apparatu) circello, notisque pro more usitatis, additiones singulas notamus. Literas etiam majusculas, & minusculas, suspensas, inversas, &c. cum vocibus non punctatis, & quæ punctas vocales habent sine literis, in quibus mysteria magna inesse credunt nonnulli cum Rabbinis, licet magni haud æstimanda, ne aliquid deesse quisquam suspicaretur, retinuimus. Punctationem etiam usitatam, licet à Maforethis textui appositam, adhibuimus; non quòd ipsorum authoritate nitatur, sed quòd ab Ecclesiâ Christiana, cui tam Hebraicorum V. Testamenti quàm Græcorum Novi fœderis voluminum cura à Deo mandata est, queque semper etiam in densissimis ignorantiæ tenebris, exemplaria Hebr. MSS. in Bibliothecis habuit, virôsque quosdam tam hujus quàm aliarum linguarum peritos, recepta est. Non enim ad Iudæos ex quo populus Dei esse desierunt, sed ad Ecclesiam Christianam pertinuit codicum Hebraorum custodiam; nec enim est punctatio vera quia à Maforethis, sed quia concordat cum vero vocalium sono, quem Spiritus

page.notes: Page ends mid-word: "Spiri-" continues on the next line with "tus" set apart at the lower right, which I have transcribed as the final catchword-like line. Several words are in italic (Exemplar, Antuerpiense, MSS., etc. are set roman with italic running text as printed); italic passages are not marked here because the scan is a reduced-resolution image and the typeface was difficult to separate reliably. Doubtful readings: "Chaser" (likely Chaser/Chasar), "circello" (possibly a printed abbreviation), "Majoram" (likely Majorem/Majora), "cū" and "etiam" in the first lines. The text is a close reading and should be checked against the scan; the Latin has been rendered in normalised u/v and i/j per instructions, but the printed Hebrew and Greek references are absent from this page.
